the morphology of the nanocrystalline zinc oxide particles plays a significant role in the electrochemical detection of hydrogen peroxide, and that the electrocatalytic performance of the nanocomposite is strongly dependent on the shape of the ZnO nanoparticles.
the morphology of the ZnO nanostructures plays an important role on the electrocatalytic behavior of the ZnO/CNT composite.

the morphology of hydrothermaly synthesized ZnO nanoparticles affects electrocatalytical activity of ZnO-MWCNT composites, and that the composites made of nanosized, semi-spherical ZnO nanoparticles are more electrocatalytically active for H2O reduction than those made of needle-like ZnO nanoparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and electrocatalytic applications of nanocomposites of ZnO nanoparticles attached to multiwalled carboxylic functionalized carbon nanotubes.
the synthesis of ZnO nanoparticles with controlled morphology and attachment to multi-walled carbon tubes for sensing applications.
the effect of morphology of ZnO on its electrocatalytic performance and the potential of this nanocomposite for use in electrochemical biosensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrocatalytic properties of ZnO/CNT composites are strongly dependent on the ZnO morphology and size.
the morphology of hydrothermaly synthesized ZnO nanoparticles affects electrocatalysis of H2O2.
morphology and size of ZnOs play an important role in electrocatalytic H2O2 sensing, with a synergistic effect of the composite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrocatalytic properties of ZnO nanoparticles attached to carbon nanotube electrodes is dependent on the morphology of the ZnO nanoparticles.
the morphology of ZnO affects the electrocatalytic properties of ZnO/MWCNTs composites for H2O detection.
ZnO nanoparticles with different morphologies have been synthesized using a facile hydrothermal approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphology of ZnO nanoparticles plays a critical role in electrocatalytic H2O2 sensing.
nanosized, semi-spherical ZnO particles have a synergistic effect with the carbon nanotubes and are more active than needle-like ZnO particles in the electrocatalysis of H2O2.
the morphology of ZnO nanoparticles synthesized via hydrothermal synthesis is an important factor in the electrocatalytic reduction of H2O2.
